cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: with two life buckets, one unit in the fresher bucket and one sale, shifting before sales creates phantom inventory next period. With one-period lead time, capacity on current orders constrains the wrong delivery period. With substitution, omitting inflow/outflow lets demand disappear.
cards.obligation: Use start-of-period inventory indexed by remaining life. New supply enters only the freshest bucket; aging removes the sales made from the bucket being shifted; only the oldest residual expires. Capacity applies to delivered inflow, while purchasing cost applies to orders. Holding cost applies to post-sales nonexpiring inventory. Demand conservation includes substitution inflow and outflow.

How does a fresher bucket become the next period's older bucket?

Which stock is charged holding cost?

cards.title: Perishable inventory and objective accounting

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: if q has no inventory but p has a high lost-sales penalty, an unbacked p-to-q flow can erase p demand at zero cost. The inbound-to-sales constraint rules out this fictitious improvement.
cards.obligation: An edge from p to q diverts p-demand to inventory of q. Bound all outbound diversion from p by p's original demand, include inbound/outbound in demand conservation, and require inbound diverted demand to be backed by actual q sales.

cards.title: Substitution direction and inventory backing

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: with lead time one and demand only in period one, a period-one order cannot serve period-one demand.
cards.obligation: Shift each order forward by its product-specific lead time; orders before the horizon are zero.

questions.prompt: How does an order placed in period s arrive?

cards.title: Lead-time timing

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: a lower link without an upper link permits a positive order with an inactive binary and avoids the fixed cost.
cards.obligation: Use one binary per product-location-period, upper-link every positive order, lower-link MOQ when active, and charge a fixed cost once per active order.

questions.prompt: How is a positive order linked to a binary activation?
How is a fixed order cost charged?

cards.title: MOQ and fixed-order activation

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: an integer order of three units violates a four-unit pack even though it is integral and above no minimum.
cards.obligation: Introduce a nonnegative integer pack count and set order quantity equal to pack size times that count.

questions.prompt: How is an order restricted to full packs?

cards.title: Pack-size integrality

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: counting incoming without outgoing duplicates every shipped unit across the network.
cards.obligation: For every product, location and period, add incoming flows and subtract outgoing flows in the fresh-inflow balance.

questions.prompt: How does a location's transshipment affect fresh inflow?

cards.title: Network transshipment balance

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: same-period returns create a circular source of inventory that can support the sale that generated the return.
cards.obligation: Returns enter the freshest bucket one period after the sale that generated them; there are no returns in the first period.

questions.prompt: Which activity generates returns in period t?

cards.title: Lagged reverse-logistics returns

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: capacity on orders does not constrain sales from existing inventory and therefore misses the operational bottleneck.
cards.obligation: Multiply product labor usage by actual sales and bound the location-period total by labor capacity.

questions.prompt: Which activity consumes retail labor capacity?

cards.title: Labor capacity

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: with positive lead time, budgeting arrivals shifts cash expenditure to the wrong period.
cards.obligation: Charge the period budget for orders placed in that period and include fixed activation costs when present.

questions.prompt: Which cash flows consume a period budget?

cards.title: Period purchasing budget

cards.counterexample_witness: Witness: per-period caps reject a plan that offsets a high-waste period with zero waste elsewhere even when the stated global fraction is satisfied.
cards.obligation: Apply one horizon-wide constraint: total physical waste cannot exceed the declared fraction of total physical demand.

questions.prompt: What is the denominator and scope of a waste percentage limit?

cards.title: Global waste limit
